question: What is the primary definition of professional accountability in nursing?

options.A: The legal right to delegate any medical task to junior staff
options.B: The requirement to work night shifts without direct supervision
options.C: The obligation to answer for one's own actions and omissions
options.D: The financial responsibility for hospital equipment maintenance

explanation: Accountability means taking ownership of your professional decisions and being answerable for the outcomes of your nursing care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is structured clinical supervision particularly critical in resource-constrained Nigerian healthcare environments?

options.A: It bridges theoretical learning with practice and protects patient safety
options.B: It removes all legal liability from the individual nurse
options.C: It replaces the need for formal nursing council registration
options.D: It guarantees automatic salary promotions after two years

explanation: In high-stress, low-resource settings, supervision ensures that standards remain high and novice nurses receive adequate guidance to protect patients from harm. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the primary difference between responsibility and accountability?

options.A: Responsibility applies only to doctors, while accountability applies only to nurses
options.B: Responsibility is legally binding, whereas accountability is purely voluntary
options.C: Accountability can be delegated entirely, but responsibility cannot
options.D: Responsibility is the obligation to perform a task, while accountability is being answerable for the outcome

explanation: You can delegate the performance of a task (responsibility), but the ultimate answerability for that choice remains with the person who delegated it (accountability). [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: A nurse follows a doctor's written prescription without question, even though the dose is ten times the safe limit, and the patient suffers toxicity. Which statement best describes the nurse's accountability?

options.A: The nurse is only accountable if they administered the drug via the intravenous route
options.B: The nurse shares accountability because professional duty requires verifying unsafe orders
options.C: The nurse is solely accountable while the physician has complete immunity
options.D: The nurse bears no accountability because they were following a medical order

explanation: Nurses are independent professionals obligated to question and verify any order that appears unsafe or outside normal clinical parameters. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which function of clinical supervision primarily deals with emotional support and managing burnout?
explanation: The restorative component focuses on the psychological well-being of the nurse, helping them cope with the emotional burdens of clinical practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: When a supervisor reviews a nurse's documentation to ensure compliance with hospital policy and professional codes of conduct, which supervisory function is being utilized?
explanation: The normative function involves monitoring and maintaining professional standards, policies, and quality control. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: What happens to accountability when a registered nurse delegates a task to a subordinate?

options.A: The registered nurse retains ultimate accountability for the overall outcome
options.B: Accountability is shared equally with the hospital administration
options.C: Accountability is eliminated entirely once the task is finished
options.D: Accountability transfers completely to the person who accepted the task

explanation: While the subordinate is responsible for performing the task correctly, the delegating nurse retains accountability for choosing to delegate it. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h4)

question: A staff nurse wants to assign vital sign collection for an unstable postoperative patient to a junior student nurse. Which of the Five Rights of Delegation is primarily violated in this scenario?
explanation: Delegating tasks involving unstable patients violates the right circumstance, as clinical instability requires higher-level professional assessment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h4)

question: Which body is statutorily empowered to regulate nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the sole legal regulatory body responsible for setting standards, licensing, and disciplining nurses and midwives across Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the primary consequence if a registered nurse is found guilty of gross professional negligence by the regulatory tribunal?

options.A: Financial compensation paid directly to the nursing union
options.B: Suspension or erasure of their name from the register
options.C: Mandatory attendance at a leadership seminar
options.D: A mandatory transfer to a rural health post

explanation: Severe professional misconduct or negligence leads to disciplinary actions by the NMCN tribunal, which can strip the practitioner of their license to practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is a major organizational barrier to effective clinical supervision in many busy hospitals?

options.A: An excess of highly trained supervisory personnel
options.B: Strict prohibition of mentorship by hospital bylaws
options.C: Complete absence of any clinical documentation
options.D: Chronic staff shortages and lack of protected time

explanation: When wards are understaffed, nurses are consumed by urgent clinical tasks, squeezing out dedicated time for supervision and mentorship. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: How does a punitive, blame-oriented institutional culture negatively impact patient safety?

options.A: It forces nurses to work faster and accomplish more tasks per shift
options.B: It automatically increases the retention rate of senior staff
options.C: It drives errors and near-misses underground, preventing organizational learning
options.D: It eliminates the need for any written nursing care plans

explanation: When staff fear harsh punishment for admitting mistakes, they hide errors instead of reporting them, robbing the team of valuable opportunities to improve safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary shift in focus when a healthcare facility adopts a modern safety culture regarding an error?

options.A: Shifting all financial penalties onto the hospital management
options.B: Ignoring minor errors to reduce paperwork
options.C: Punishing the entire shift team regardless of involvement
options.D: Moving from blame toward analyzing systemic root causes

explanation: A true safety culture looks beyond individual fault to identify and fix underlying system flaws that permitted the error to occur. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h7)

question: Which nursing activity directly contributes to continuous quality improvement on a clinical ward?

options.A: Refusing to participate in interprofessional team meetings
options.B: Participating in regular clinical audits and reflective practice
options.C: Avoiding documentation of near-misses to save time
options.D: Delegating all supervisory duties to non-nursing staff

explanation: Clinical audits and reflection allow nurses to systematically evaluate care practices, identify gaps, and implement targeted improvements. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h7)
